runtimeLimitations: Running image is locally built memos-dev-memos, not a verified memtensor/memos:2.0.30 image.
Source reports package 2.0.30; installed package metadata is absent. Docker files differ locally; API sources are unmodified.
No auth in this server_api OpenAPI; network isolation is required.
Health reports HTTP API version 1.0.1 and does not verify databases or model readiness.
Add invokes embedding and schedules further processing even in sync/fast mode; paid-model live tests were not run.
Upstream add logs full request bodies; remove/redact that logging before production use.
Deletion response reports success/failure but no deletion count.
get_memory exports text memories and optional types, not complete database/user/cube administrative state.
The adapter uses async add to preserve the supplied task_id; task status is checked separately. A missing task is an error, not proof of completion.

create_cube validates owner_id against upstream's own UserManager and answers 400 for an owner it does not know. memOsNamespace derives an opaque owner id that nothing registers, so this call fails against a real engine until the migration registers users first. add does not perform that check and materializes the cube implicitly today.

Async feedback returns data: [[]] — an empty process record the handler still wraps in a list — and upstream logs and swallows a failed scheduler submission while returning that same body. An accepted feedback and a dropped one are indistinguishable in the response; only the task id can separate them afterwards.
feedback resolves cube ids to [user_id] when writable_cube_ids is absent, which is outside our namespace. The adapter always sends the list; an omission upstream would be a silent cross-scope write.
runtimeSourceHashEvidence: The first two SHA-256 values matched the checked-out upstream source and the running container; this is not image attestation. The three added for the derived endpoints were taken from the tarball at sourceCommit only — no container was running when they were read — and the two container-verified hashes in the same tarball still match, which is what ties the tarball to the observed server.
deploymentAcceptance: Deploy a dedicated engine from an attested 2.0.30 source/image, with immutable source and no reload flag.
Use a private network reachable only by the EviMed control plane, excluding all DSH runtime containers. The raw API has no authentication.
Provision persistent graph/vector stores, scheduler Redis, writable local file storage, and model endpoints; validate actual selected backends and dimensions against src/memos/api/config.py.
Remove full request-body logging in upstream AddHandler and SingleCubeView before processing user memory.

Run the opt-in disposable live contract only after authorization for embedding/model calls. It verifies storage, task completion, provenance, cross-account/project isolation, scoped deletion, account-wide deletion, and cleanup.

Before migrating retained product documents, reconcile every product entryId/provenanceId with engine IDs, including failures and partial writes; verify restart persistence and backup/restore separately.
Register each derived owner id with the engine's UserManager before calling create_cube, and decide whether the migration creates cubes explicitly or keeps relying on implicit creation by add.
Confirm on a live engine that a feedback task id appears in /product/scheduler/status, since the feedback response itself cannot report a dropped submission.
